messages:
maria: Heads up — provisioning in ap-southeast-1 hit a keystore latency spike around 02:15 UTC. GPU node launches stuck in Pending and a bunch of KMS timeouts seen. cc @elena @aj

aj: I can repro the KMS timeouts, seeing 503/504s to kms-prod-apac. Launch requests hang on `AttachKey` in the bootstrap logs.

elena: Any recent IAM/KMS policy pushes to apac? I didn't touch the keystore policies this morning.

maria: We did a small keystore policy tweak last night to add a deny for cross-account assume on test roles, but that was in eu. Not sure it should affect apac.

aj: grabbing logs from the node provisioner — attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-18T02:14:56Z provisioner ERROR attach_kms_key: rpc deadline exceeded
2026-03-18T02:15:01Z kms-client WARN 503 Service Unavailable
```


devex_jin: sre-bot just opened INC-2026-2345 and pinged platform oncall. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-2345 :white_flag:

sre-bot: Incident created by automation: INC-2026-2345 — ap-southeast-1 keystore latency impacting GPU provisioning. Priority P1.

elena: I'm seeing increased VPC NAT gateway SNAT exhaustion in that region around the same time — many KMS calls from provisioner are going through the nat pool and queueing. Could be capacity + KMS retries amplifying.

aj: Good catch. NAT metrics show connections spiking 4x at 02:12. We also had a regional CNCF mirror sync earlier which might have burst egress.

maria: Action plan proposal: 1) throttle provisioner concurrency in apac, 2) rotate to a different NAT gateway / escalate for additional SNAT capacity, 3) fallback: use cached key material for warm nodes if we can. Thoughts?

elena: +1 for throttling and adding NAT. For cached keys — that's sensitive, need security approval before changing key caching TTL.

devex_jin: For immediate mitigation I pushed a concurrency limit to 5 for the apac provisioner (rolling config). That reduced the error rate in the next 5m.

aj: After throttling errors dropped ~70%, node launches trickling through. However cost signal: autoscaler retried and launched extra spot attempts; estimate ~3k USD extra spend for last 24h in apac.

maria: Noted. We'll include the overspend in the incident timeline for cost review.

elena: Long-term: request to platform to provision a second NAT gateway pair for apac and increase SNAT port allocation. I'll open a ticket to infra-ops. Also need an audit log correlation: which role made the policy tweak and when.
\mj (typo)

aj: audit log snippet shows policy change by `ops:policy-bot` at 2026-03-17T23:40Z affecting eu-only ARNs — doesn't look like a direct cause. Still, we should verify if any cross-region replication of policy happened.

maria: Can we add a runbook step for 'provisioner KMS timeouts' to try NAT failover before rolling keystore changes? Saves the knee-jerk rollback.

elena: agree — and add a compliance check: any caching/TTL change needs a security signoff + KMS key usage review.

devex_jin: I'll draft the runbook update and the post-incident RCA note. Also creating a short canary to validate keystore calls after any policy change.

sre-bot: Status update: mitigation applied (provisioner throttling + NAT failover queued). Monitoring shows stabilizing.

maria: Thanks all. After stabilization let's run a controlled replay: 50 node launches via canary path to verify cold attach path works end-to-end and confirm no audit gaps.

elena: I'll own the audit correlation and NAT request. Assigning to infra-ops ticket INF-APAC-482.

aj: I'll follow up with cost estimate for the extra spot churn and include the cost mitigation suggestions (burst limits, better backoff).

maria: Closing here — we'll update thread with RCA link when available. :white_check_mark:
